whatIsIt.eli5: A cheaper way to make the picture smaller: first change the kinds of notes, then shrink the picture.
whatIsIt.simple: YOLOv10's downsampling block: a 1×1 Conv changes the number of channels, then a depthwise 3×3 Conv with stride 2 halves the size.
whatIsIt.engineer: SCDown: Conv(c1, c2, 1) → Conv(c2, c2, k, s, g=c2, act=False).

whyExists.eli5: Doing two simple jobs one after another is cheaper than one big job.
whyExists.simple: A normal 3×3 stride-2 Conv does both jobs (more channels, smaller map) at once, which is costly. Splitting them saves a lot of parameters and compute.
whyExists.engineer: Decoupling channel mixing (pointwise) from spatial reduction (depthwise) reduces cost from O(9·c1·c2) to O(c1·c2 + 9·c2) per position (paper §3.2).

eli5: Shrink each kind on its own.
simple: Depthwise k×k Conv, stride 2: each channel is shrunk on its own.
engineer: No activation on the depthwise conv.

example.eli5: In YOLOv10n, a 128-note map is made half as big with far fewer learned numbers than a normal step.
example.simple: YOLOv10n layer 5: 64 → 128 channels, 80×80 → 40×40, 9,856 parameters. YOLOv8n's equivalent Conv (layer 5) has 73,984.

typicalPositions.eli5: Where the picture gets smaller in the later part of the backbone and neck.
typicalPositions.simple: Replaces the stride-2 Convs at P4, P5 and the last PAN step in YOLOv10.
